channel.title: GetDiscoverable.io — Notes on being found
channel.description: Plain-English writing on SEO, AEO, and GEO — how a business gets found by search engines and AI assistants. By Zillah Bahar.

item.title: How to Write a Tasting Note an AI Will Actually Quote
item.description: Most tasting notes are written to sound beautiful. To get your wine recommended by AI, they need to be written to be read by a machine. The difference, with a before-and-after.

item.title: The Winery Website Checklist for Getting Found by AI
item.description: When a buyer asks an assistant to recommend a wine, some wineries get named and others vanish. Six fixable checks — in plain English — to make your winery the one AI names.

item.title: I Built This Site to Be Found by AI. Here's Exactly What I Did.
item.description: A transparent, plain-English teardown of everything I did to make this site discoverable by search engines and AI — every move, why it matters to a machine, and the honest timeline.

item.title: How Do Regulated Brands Get Found by AI?
item.description: The compliance habits that keep you legal — age walls, hedged copy, facts buried in PDFs — are often what makes you invisible to AI. How to fix it without crossing a line.

item.title: How Do I Make My Business Discoverable on AI?
item.description: The plain-English answer — six fixable steps to become the brand an AI assistant names when a buyer asks, no ad budget required.

item.title: How to Tell If AI Can't See Your Brand
item.description: When a buyer asks ChatGPT to recommend something in your category, does your brand come up? A seven-point self-check you can run in ten minutes — and the fix for each.

item.title: SEO vs AEO vs GEO: What's the Difference?
item.description: A plain-English guide to the three ways people and AI find you online in 2026 — search engines, answer engines, and generative engines — and why you can no longer optimize for only the first.

item.title: How I Got COLAClear Cited by Name in Google's AI Overview
item.description: A first-person account of the work behind a by-name AI citation — writing for real questions, machine-readable signals (schema.org, llms.txt), AI-crawler access, and earned authority. No budget, no team.

item.title: Why AI Recommends Some Wineries by Name — and Never Mentions Yours
item.description: When a buyer asks ChatGPT for a great bottle, some wineries get named and others vanish. What separates them — machine-readable text, one consistent name, structured data, open crawler access — and how to fix it.
